name: Elizaphan
title: Levitical leader from the Uzziel clan
summary: Elizaphan (also known as Elzaphan) was the son of Uzziel and grandson of Kohath from the tribe of Levi. He was appointed by Moses as chief over the clans of the Kohathites and played an important role during the wilderness journey, including carrying away the bodies of Nadab and Abihu after their unauthorized offering to the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as chief over the Kohathites
keyEvents.description: Moses appointed Elizaphan, son of Uzziel, to lead the clans of the Kohathites. He was given responsibility for leading this Levitical group during the wilderness journey.

keyEvents.title: Tasks of the Kohathites at the tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Elizaphan's clan, the Kohathites, were responsible for caring for the most holy items in the tabernacle, including the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the sacred utensils.

keyEvents.title: Carrying Away Nadab and Abihu
keyEvents.description: After Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord because they offered unauthorized fire, Moses commanded that Elizaphan and his brother Mishael carry their bodies out of the camp.

keyEvents.title: Counting of the Kohathites in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: During the census in the wilderness, the Kohathites, whom Elizaphan led, were counted and registered for their service at the tabernacle. The number of men from one month old and upward was 8600.

keyEvents.title: Descendants in David's Time
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Elizaphan are mentioned in connection with King David's organization of Levitical service, where they participated in bringing the ark of the covenant to Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Descendants in the time of Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: During King Hezekiah's religious reforms, the descendants of Elizaphan took part in cleansing the temple and restoring worship.
